candidate.answerReason: Three equal gaps span 60 feet, so each gap is 20 feet. Six trees span five gaps, totaling 100 feet and matching choice B.

methods.label: Count the spaces between trees
methods.explanation:
Equal spacing suggests counting the gaps between trees. From the first tree to the fourth there are \(3\) gaps, so each gap measures
\[
60\div3=20\text{ feet}.
\]
From the first tree to the sixth and last tree there are \(5\) gaps. Thus the distance is
\[
5\times20=100\text{ feet},
\]
choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary endpoint-and-gap counting, division, and multiplication.

candidate.annotationRationale: The key target is distinguishing the number of trees from the number of intervening gaps. Equal-sharing division finds one gap, and multiplication combines five equal gaps.
